summary: Hamilton Island Airport serves as the main gateway to the Whitsunday Islands, a renowned archipelago off the central Queensland coast. It was rebranded as Great Barrier Reef Airport in 2021 to highlight its proximity to one of the world's most iconic natural wonders. The airport sits on Hamilton Island itself, surrounded by turquoise Coral Sea waters, and is known for offering one of the most scenic landings in Australian aviation.
faqs:
Q: Is Hamilton Island Airport on the same island as the resort?
A: Yes, the airport is located directly on Hamilton Island, a short walk or shuttle ride from the main resort, marina, and accommodation areas.

Q: Which airlines fly into Hamilton Island Airport?
A: Qantas and Virgin Australia operate regular services from mainland hubs such as Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, and Cairns.

Q: Are there customs and immigration facilities at the airport?
A: No, Hamilton Island is a domestic-only airport. International travelers must clear customs at a mainland port before connecting.

Q: How far is the airport from Whitehaven Beach?
A: Whitehaven Beach is not on Hamilton Island itself; it is reached by boat or helicopter transfer, typically taking 30 to 75 minutes from the island marina.
transport_tips: Most visitors arrange transfers through their accommodation, with complimentary shuttle buses or golf buggies commonly available on the island. Alternatively, ferry services connect Hamilton Island to Airlie Beach on the mainland. Taxis and pre-booked private transfers operate from the small terminal, but renting a golf buggy is a popular and practical way to get around the island.
local_tip: Bring only what you need for the day in your hand luggage, as checked baggage handling on the small propeller aircraft can be slow and luggage occasionally arrives on later flights.
